title: Samsung Announces Android 17 Rollout: Galaxy Phones & Tablets List Confirmed by 9to5Google
body:
Samsung has unveiled the first wave of Galaxy smartphones and tablets that will receive the company’s upcoming Android 17‑based One UI 9 update, confirming that a broad swath of its flagship and mid‑range lineup will be refreshed with the new software in the months ahead. The announcement, which lists devices confirmed for at least one regional rollout, gives consumers and industry watchers a clearer picture of Samsung’s post‑Android 17 roadmap and signals the company’s commitment to extending support across its extensive hardware portfolio.

The confirmed roster spans the latest premium models and several popular mid‑tier devices. Flagship phones such as the Galaxy S24, S24+, and S24 Ultra are slated to receive One UI 9, as are the Galaxy Z Fold 5 and Z Flip 5, Samsung’s leading foldable offerings. In the mid‑range segment, the Galaxy A54, A74 and A94 will also be upgraded, while the Galaxy Tab S9 series—including the S9+, S9 Ultra and the standard S9—will join the update schedule. Samsung noted that the list reflects devices that will see the update in at least one market, implying a staggered global rollout that could extend to additional regions over time.

One UI 9 builds on Android 17’s new capabilities, promising a more refined user experience, enhanced privacy controls and deeper integration with Samsung’s ecosystem of wearables, smart TVs and appliances. Among the headline features are a redesigned notification shade, a revamped quick settings panel, and more granular permission settings that give users tighter control over data access. Samsung also highlighted improvements to its AI‑driven Bixby assistant and the introduction of “Smart Widgets,” which aim to deliver contextual information at a glance without opening apps. For devices with high‑refresh‑rate displays, the update will enable smoother animations and better battery management through adaptive refresh rate tuning.

The timing of the rollout aligns with Samsung’s broader strategy to differentiate itself in a crowded Android market by offering longer software lifecycles. While Google typically promises three years of Android version updates for its Pixel line, Samsung has been extending its support window to five years for many of its newer devices. This move not only bolsters consumer confidence but also positions Samsung as a viable alternative for users who prioritize longevity and security. Analysts note that the inclusion of mid‑range models like the A54 and A74 reflects Samsung’s effort to democratize premium experiences, ensuring that a larger share of its user base benefits from the latest Android innovations.

Industry experts also see the announcement as a bellwether for the competitive dynamics of the upcoming Android 17 release. By confirming a substantial portion of its lineup ahead of the official OS launch, Samsung is signaling confidence in the stability and performance of Android 17, while also giving developers a clearer timeline for testing and optimization. The update’s rollout will likely influence the market share battle with rivals such as Google’s Pixel, Xiaomi’s Mi series, and Apple’s iOS ecosystem, especially as consumers weigh the value of extended software support against hardware specifications.

Looking ahead, Samsung is expected to continue expanding the One UI 9 rollout to additional devices, possibly including older flagships that have not yet been confirmed. The company’s roadmap suggests a phased approach, with early updates rolling out in key markets like the United States, South Korea and parts of Europe before reaching emerging regions. As the Android 17 platform gains traction, Samsung’s extensive update schedule could set a new benchmark for Android OEMs, reinforcing its leadership in delivering sustained software value across a diverse device portfolio.
